adaptation_action: The project combined technical planning with robust community engagement to build local resilience to sea level rise. Key strategies included developing practical tools like vulnerability maps and implementation frameworks, integrating sea level rise into Shoreline Master Programs, and facilitating collaborative workshops. These workshops brought together residents, local agencies, and scientists to ensure the strategies reflected both scientific understanding and community priorities.

outcomes: The Island County Sea Level Rise Strategy Study resulted in adaptable planning tools, including vulnerability maps and adaptation frameworks, that can support informed decision-making across various sectors. Overall, the project was able to successfully integrate sea level rise data within shoreline planning and fostered stronger collaborative networks between local agencies and community members. As a result, Island County is better equipped to prepare for and respond to future coastal flooding and sea level rise impacts.

summary: The Island County Sea Level Rise Strategy Study aimed to enhance flood preparedness and resilience by providing an actionable framework to strengthen the county’s coastlines, infrastructure, and ecosystems in the face of rising seas. A key objective was to integrate adaptation strategies into Shoreline Master Programs and other planning documents, ensuring that technical data translated effectively into policy. The project also focused on developing practical tools, such as vulnerability maps and implementation frameworks, to support local departments in incorporating sea level rise into everyday decision-making. Through collaborative workshops and public outreach, the study grounded its recommendations in both scientific insight and community values using a co-productive approach.
title: Island County Sea Level Rise Strategy Study
transferability: This project demonstrated how multi-dimensional co-production strategies can foster effective collaboration among communities, organizations, scientific institutions, and government agencies.
